payload.previous_proof_nl: Let x be any real number. By definition, floor(x) is the greatest integer less than or equal to x. Therefore floor(x) is itself less than or equal to x. Since x was arbitrary, this holds for every real number x.

payload.statement_nl: For every real number x, floor(x) ≤ x.

result_payload.addressed_previous_feedback: I retained the same direct argument but made the justification explicit: by definition of floor, it is the greatest integer not exceeding x, so the inequality follows immediately for arbitrary real x.
result_payload.proof_nl: Let x be an arbitrary real number. By definition, floor(x) is the greatest integer less than or equal to x. In particular, floor(x) itself is an integer that does not exceed x, so floor(x) ≤ x. Since x was arbitrary, this holds for every real number x.
result_payload.proof_summary: Directly from the defining property of the floor function: floor(x) is the greatest integer ≤ x, hence floor(x) ≤ x for all real x.

used_external_facts: Definition of the floor function as the greatest integer less than or equal to a real number
